text: Why does `ArrayList` grow by roughly half rather than by a fixed number of slots?
choices: Because proportional growth makes `add` constant time when averaged over many calls, while fixed growth makes it linear.
Because copying is cheaper when the new array is a multiple of the old one's size.
Because a fixed increment would waste memory on large lists.
Because the JVM allocates in power-of-two blocks, so proportional growth matches the allocator.
explanation: Doubling to capacity n copies about n elements in total across n additions — fewer than one copy per add on average, which is Chapter 32's amortised O(1) and Chapter 17's sum of powers of two. Growing by a constant 10 instead would copy roughly n²/20 elements, making list construction quadratic. The difference between a good dynamic array and a catastrophic one is which growth rule was chosen.
